cards.explanation: The answer is that Laban's sons say Jacob built all his wealth off their father. Laban's sons, the sons of Jacob's father-in-law, say, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.” (Genesis 31:1) That's what reaches Jacob's ears. It's like finding out your name came up in a meeting you weren't invited to.

The answer is True. It's written right on Laban's face. The text says, “And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.” (Genesis 31:2) Countenance just means the look on his face. Some faces don't need a caption.

The answer is that the LORD tells Jacob to go back to the land of his fathers. The LORD says, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.” (Genesis 31:3) It's a clear instruction with a promise attached. Jacob doesn't have to figure out the next step on his own.

The answer is True, and that promise matters. The LORD ends His command with, “…and I will be with you.” (Genesis 31:3) Jacob is told where to go, and he's also told he won't be going alone. That's a good deal on any road trip.

The answer is the God of his father. Jacob starts by saying he can see that Laban's attitude toward him has changed. Then he turns it around: “…the God of my father has been with me.” (Genesis 31:5) Rachel and Leah are the ones hearing this out in the field. Jacob puts God right next to the bad news.
The answer is ten. Jacob says Laban “…has cheated me and changed my wages ten times…” (Genesis 31:7) Ten times, friends! At some point that's not a mistake in the paperwork, it's a hobby.
The answer is False. Jacob says, “…God has not allowed him to harm me.” (Genesis 31:7) He doesn't hide that Laban cheated him and changed his wages. But he says God stood between him and the harm.

The answer is livestock. Jacob says, “Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.” (Genesis 31:9) He says it was God's doing. That's how he explains to his wives where his flocks came from.

The answer is that the males are all streaked or spotted or speckled. The angel says, “Look up… and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled.” (Genesis 31:12) That's the same kind of markings Jacob mentioned to his wives. In the dream, he's told to look up and see it.
The answer is all that Laban has done to Jacob. The angel says, “for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.” (Genesis 31:12) Nothing Laban did slipped past unseen. Jacob hears that in the dream.
The answer is False. The angel says, “Now get up, leave this land at once, and return to your native land.” (Genesis 31:13) There's no mention of waiting for Laban's blessing. The word is “at once.”
The answer is outsiders. Rachel and Leah ask, “Are we not regarded by him as outsiders?” (Genesis 31:15) They say it about their own father, Laban. It stings when family treats you like a stranger.

The answer is that their father sold them and wasted the money. They say, “Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.” (Genesis 31:15) Squandered means spent it away. They're laying out what their father did, and it's a lot.

The answer is True. Rachel and Leah say, “Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children.” (Genesis 31:16) They see it as theirs and their children's. And they say God is the one who took it from their father.

The answer is that they tell Jacob to do whatever God has told him. They finish with, “So do whatever God has told you.” (Genesis 31:16) Rachel and Leah put it plainly. Jacob has his answer from his wives, and God's word is already on the table.

The answer is to his father Isaac in Canaan. The text says he drove his livestock “…to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.” (Genesis 31:18) Isaac is Jacob's father. It's a long trip with a lot of animals.
The answer is Rachel. The text says, “…Rachel stole her father’s household idols.” (Genesis 31:19) Rachel is Jacob's wife and Laban's daughter. She took them while Laban was away shearing his sheep.

The answer is that he runs off without telling Laban. The text says, “…Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.” (Genesis 31:20) The deception here is silence. He just left without a word.

The answer is the Euphrates. The text says Jacob “…crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.” (Genesis 31:21) A big river crossing with camels and a whole flock is no small thing. Imagine the splashing.
